newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on flood talk, exports.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on flood talk, exports.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed higher on concerns about potential flooding this spring in the U.S. Midwest, especially in the Northern Midwest spring wheat growing region, traders said.
Bullish input from the export sector and a strong tone in the CBOT soy complex also were cited along with bullish technical signals.
"Export sales this morning was viewed as very bullish," a floor trader said.
USDA early Thursday released its weekly export report and nearly every major commodity received renewed bullish input.
The government said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended March 13 totaled 449,100 tonnes, above expectations for 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Technical traders also cited bullish signals.
"Technicals changed for wheat, I think part of it was technical," a trader said.

Technicians early Thursday said the four- and 20-day moving averages were bullish for KCBT May wheat and the market early Thursday broke above first resistance in the May at $4.23 per bushel to touch a session high of $4.28. Second resistance was pegged by chartists at $4.35.

Traders said there was some concern about potential water-damage to portions of the U.S. winter wheat crop but the key focal point was the U.S. spring wheat growing region and the possibility of planting delays there.
"That is still a problem especially in northern Minnesota and areas in the Dakotas. They still have a lot of snow on the ground," a trader said.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 4-3/4 to 12 cents per bushel higher, with May up 4-3/4 at $4.23-1/4. July was up 5-3/4 at $3.92-1/4.
